document.title: Sophia Real-Time Platform — Provider-Neutral Core and Complete Sophia Admin Scope
document.artifactType: Codex task specification, not a native Codex configuration file
document.evidenceBoundary: The attached architecture JSON was reviewed in full. Repository files, branches, live services, databases, SDK versions, credentials and production behavior were not accessed or executed. Current-state findings below are baseline-reported, not independently code-verified. Codex must inspect the actual working trees first.
document.scope: Incremental evolution of the existing Angular frontend, NestJS runtime, Express Business Manager and existing workers. Preserve real estate as an optional business pack. Exclude the existing migration/student-agency implementation from the new product. Explicit Sophia Admin control plane covering all sixteen requested modules, with separately gated commercial billing.

validatedAmendments.reason: Production-readiness inspection proved that the deployed database URL authenticates as neondb_owner and merely starts with SET ROLE sophia_runtime_app. The session_user therefore retains owner authority and can RESET ROLE, so this is not a genuine least-privilege runtime credential. Inspection also found subscription/invoice observations and lifecycle SQL still carry sandbox assumptions that must be separated before live evidence can coexist safely.
changes: Split P6-A06C into four explicit gates: C1 genuine Neon non-owner login cutover, C2 dormant live-mode adapter and environment-separated persistence, C3 live-resource verification without Checkout, and C4 a separate real-charge activation decision.
Require a LOGIN role whose session_user is not the owner, has no BYPASSRLS or role-creation privileges, and may SET ROLE only to the existing NOLOGIN sophia_runtime_app capability role.
Keep live Checkout disabled by default even when live credentials and resources are configured. Portal, callback and reconciliation readiness must not imply charge authority.
Do not reuse sandbox customer, Checkout, subscription, invoice or webhook identities in live mode; persistence and uniqueness must include provider_environment throughout.
validatedAmendments.approvedBy: User agreement to replace the owner-backed connection, add live-mode support, configure live resources and decide charge activation explicitly

validatedAmendments.reason: A real Stripe sandbox subscription lifecycle was completed against the deployed Sophia Runtime. The first authoritative reconciliation exposed that the shared subscription/invoice identity trigger accessed table-specific record fields in boolean expressions and failed on the other table. The transaction rolled back, migration 035 replaced the trigger with table-routed nested branches, and reconciliation then completed with one active subscription and one paid AUD invoice.
changes: Mark P6-A06B complete with evidence from a provider-hosted AUD 1 monthly Checkout, the issued-intent-matched signed callback, sandbox customer binding, one active subscription, one paid invoice, hosted portal creation and authoritative reconciliation.
Add migration 035 to repair table-specific billing reference trigger routing while preserving immutable tenant/provider/reference identities and monotonic observation revisions.

Keep the Business Manager recent-MFA gate unchanged. The sandbox proof used a bounded operator invocation of the same lifecycle service because the current Business Manager identity contract still provides no mfaVerifiedAt evidence.
Keep live charge activation in P6-A06C. Sandbox success, available production credentials and deployed Admin UI do not authorize or enable live Checkout.
validatedAmendments.approvedBy: User instruction to complete the sandbox lifecycle and maintain the plan when runtime evidence identifies a necessary correction

validatedAmendments.reason: The operator confirmed that Stripe payments have already been exercised with test credentials and that production credentials are available outside the repository. Stripe API keys are account-scoped, so a separate Sophia-only API key is not a sound isolation requirement. The repository still contains no evidence of a Sophia recurring-subscription sandbox run and no live Sophia configuration, so neither P6-A06B nor production activation can be marked complete from the existing one-time payment test.
changes: Replace the dedicated-credential requirement with Sophia-specific configuration and resources: SOPHIA_BILLING_* secret injection, recurring Product/Price mappings, metadata namespace, webhook destination/signing secret and customer portal configuration. The account credential may be shared when access policy permits, but legacy environment-variable fallback and legacy Toolkit/video product reuse remain prohibited.

Keep P6-A06B as the evidence-backed Sophia recurring-subscription test-mode run. Existing generic or one-time Stripe payment evidence does not substitute for Checkout subscription, signed callback, invoice, portal and reconciliation evidence.

Treat live mode as a separate production-activation slice after P6-A06B. It requires explicit live configuration, deployed HTTPS return/webhook URLs, approved live recurring Price mappings, verified recent-MFA operator access and an explicit decision to enable charge-creating Checkout.
Do not store production Stripe secrets in the repository or plan. Inject them through the deployment secret manager and record only opaque resource identifiers and redacted verification evidence.
validatedAmendments.approvedBy: User clarification that test payments have been exercised and production credentials are now available, together with the standing instruction to correct the plan when a better design is identified

validatedAmendments.reason: Repository inspection found a Stripe test credential only in the legacy Business Manager process for unrelated one-time Toolkit/video products. Sophia Runtime has no dedicated subscription credential, webhook secret, approved recurring Price mapping, portal configuration or platform commercial operator. Reusing those product objects or inventing a recurring price would violate the namespace and commercial-authority boundaries established in P6-A05.
changes: Split P6-A06 into P6-A06A for a concrete but dormant Stripe sandbox adapter, signed payload-free webhook lifecycle, tenant/customer routing, replay and out-of-order protection, authoritative reconciliation, hosted-action APIs and Admin readiness UI; P6-A06B remains the separately configured sandbox end-to-end proof.

Require Sophia-specific environment names, a test-mode secret key, signing secret, explicit recurring Price mapping and hosted return URLs before the adapter reports sandbox availability. Never fall back to the legacy STRIPE_SECRET_KEY or reuse Toolkit/video product metadata.

Fail closed unless the mapped Stripe test Price exactly matches the approved plan currency, fixed base amount and interval. The first hosted lifecycle supports fixed recurring plans with no usage-overage lines and tax marked not applicable; metered usage and tax collection require a later approved provider design rather than silent underbilling or tax invention.
Keep sandbox subscription/invoice state as provider evidence only. It must not publish plans, assign commercial entitlements, enable production admission or create a live charge.
Store no raw webhook or card data. Persist only opaque provider references, event identity/type/time, a SHA-256 payload digest and bounded processing evidence under forced tenant RLS.
Protect provider customer, subscription, invoice and webhook identities with database triggers; observations may advance only monotonically and a received webhook may be finalized once.

Persist an opaque tenant/plan-bound Checkout reservation before the idempotent provider call, attach the returned provider Session through a one-way transition, and require checkout.session.completed to match that issued Session before binding a customer; signed metadata alone is not initiation authority.

Reserve one active tenant Checkout request before provider I/O, retain ambiguous outcomes for same-key recovery and block a second request from creating a parallel subscription; the Admin workspace reuses the active request identity rather than guessing a new one.

Use provider idempotency keys plus database event uniqueness, process supported events from current authoritative provider state where possible, and apply observations only when they are not older than the stored state.
Keep checkout, portal and reconciliation behind billing.manage and recent MFA; keep the signed provider callback separate from browser/Admin authentication.

validatedAmendments.reason: Repository inspection found duplicated v1/v2 count-then-act admission checks that can oversubscribe during concurrent requests. It also found the immutable v2 SessionPlan maximumToolCalls session-total limit was being treated as a per-minute limit, which permits additional calls after the window rolls over. Provider-cost evidence may span currencies and remains an estimate, so a tenant threshold cannot safely become a billing balance or hard admission decision.
changes: Centralize v1/v2 admission in one Runtime service and use transaction-scoped advisory locks plus durable short-lived reservations so concurrent session and tool admissions cannot pass the same remaining slot.

Treat the configured platform limits and any assigned commercial entitlements as upper bounds. A tenant guardrail may select a value at or below that ceiling and may be relaxed only within the current ceiling; it cannot raise an entitlement or mutate a commercial assignment.
Enforce the v2 SessionPlan maximumToolCalls as a total per-session ceiling, separately from the platform/tenant per-minute tool rate.

Expose provider-cost thresholds as calendar-UTC, single-currency estimate alerts only. They create no charge, balance, entitlement change or admission denial, and unavailable/mixed evidence remains explicit.
Audit optimistic guardrail changes under usage.limits.manage with recent MFA and retain server-side enforcement even though navigation visibility is presentation-only.

validatedAmendments.reason: Repository inspection found only unrelated one-time Stripe payment flows for Toolkit/video purchases, not a Sophia subscription authority. The fixed tenant Billing Administrator role also cannot safely publish platform rate cards or assign its own entitlements, and no authenticated platform billing operator exists. Treating provider cost estimates as a bill or exposing self-assignment would weaken commercial and authorization boundaries.
changes: Split P6-A05 into P6-A05A for the commercial/usage read model, disabled BillingProvider contract, no-charge preview and Admin workspace, followed by P6-A05B for downward-only tenant guardrails and admission enforcement.

Persist versioned platform commercial definitions, tenant assignments and external billing references separately from provider usage, but grant the Runtime role read-only access and expose no tenant mutation API for plan publication or assignment.

Leave every commercial table empty until separately authorised platform provisioning supplies approved prices, currency, tax and overage policy; an absent assignment produces an explicit unavailable preview, never inferred zero pricing.

Keep existing Toolkit/video Stripe objects and callbacks outside the Sophia namespace. Define a disabled provider-neutral billing port now; concrete hosted checkout, portal, signed callbacks and sandbox lifecycle remain P6-A06.
Allow P6-A05B tenant controls only to lower platform hard caps or configure non-enforcing alerts; raising entitlements or changing commercial assignment requires future platform authority and audit.
Keep published pricing/content immutable while allowing the explicit lifecycle-only published-to-retired transition; retired versions remain immutable.

validatedAmendments.reason: Canonical session, workflow and escalation lifecycle rows are intentionally mutable. A render-on-access analytics manifest could therefore return different counts from the snapshot approved at creation, while persisting raw conversation content would be unnecessary. Repository role inspection also found analytics.export declared but unreachable from every fixed role.
changes: Persist only the bounded aggregate analytics snapshot, registry definitions and coverage/cost summary for 24 hours; never include raw conversation, tool input/output, transcript, audio or personal content.

Digest the immutable snapshot with SHA-256, enforce a 5,000-point and 5 MiB bound, and scrub the stored aggregate document when the export expires while retaining immutable manifest/digest/access evidence.

Keep analytics.read and analytics.export distinct. Grant both to Organisation Owner so the export path is reachable; Operations Member and Read-only Auditor retain analytics.read without export authority.
Keep analytics export outside the recent-MFA set because it contains bounded aggregate operational evidence only; conversation-content and audit exports retain their stronger existing MFA boundaries.
Run multi-query dashboard aggregation inside a tenant-scoped repeatable-read, read-only transaction so one dashboard/export cannot mix source states from different committed database snapshots.

Expose the dashboard with honest empty, missing-attribution, timezone-fallback, source-confirmed and estimate states; do not add a charting dependency when accessible tables and compact native bars are sufficient.
validatedAmendments.approvedBy: User instruction to evaluate and update the plan when repository evidence identifies a safer or more accurate design

validatedAmendments.reason: Repository validation found deduplicated canonical session, tool, workflow, escalation and provider-usage records, but no universal business conversion event and no safe pack-neutral way to infer one from a closed session or attempted action. A second persisted aggregate would introduce freshness/reconciliation state before any scale evidence requires it. Organisation timezone is optional free-form metadata, and provider cost estimates can span currencies/table versions that must not be converted or presented as customer revenue.
changes: Split P6-A03 into P6-A03A for a versioned declarative metric registry plus tenant/timezone-bounded on-demand aggregation, followed by P6-A03B for expiring exports and the Angular dashboard.

Treat session lifecycle, attempts, failures and escalations as operational observations; label a business outcome source-confirmed only when a compiled pack declares a canonical tool/workflow outcome source.
Allow business packs to declare bounded metric definitions, never SQL or executable aggregation logic; core compiles only approved source kinds.

Aggregate directly from deduplicated canonical rows for the current scale, expose freshness/coverage, and defer materialized aggregates until measured query volume justifies a reconciliation lifecycle.

Use the tenant's valid IANA timezone or UTC with an explicit fallback warning. Keep cost estimates separated by currency, table version and measurement status; perform no conversion and claim no revenue, savings or causal lift.
validatedAmendments.approvedBy: User instruction to evaluate and update the plan when repository evidence identifies a safer or more accurate design

validatedAmendments.reason: Repository validation found no private conversation-export object store or export worker, while controlled conversation content remains subject to later retention expiry and privacy redaction. Persisting a generated document in PostgreSQL would create an untracked second copy of sensitive content; labelling a synchronous database operation asynchronous would create false operational evidence.
changes: Replace the assumed asynchronous stored-document export with a bounded expiring manifest that pins tenant, conversation, scope, item limit and as-of cutoff but stores no conversation document.
Render JSON only on authorised access, re-evaluating current privacy/retention state so later redaction or expiry cannot be bypassed by an earlier manifest.

Require conversations.export with recent MFA for every export and additionally require conversations.read_content for content-scoped creation and download; export authority alone can produce metadata only.
Expire manifests after 24 hours, audit creation/access with a SHA-256 digest and preserve immutable manifest identity/access evidence under forced RLS.
Keep transcript and audio absent from exports while no consent-bound retained asset exists; the Angular workspace exposes no playback control.
validatedAmendments.approvedBy: User instruction to evaluate and update the plan when repository evidence identifies a safer or more accurate design

validatedAmendments.reason: Repository validation found that the escalation operations inbox is already delivered, while the Runtime deliberately disables full-transcript and raw-audio persistence and has no retained transcript/audio object model. Treating generic event payloads or provider logs as a transcript, or exposing a playback control without a consent-bound retained asset, would invent unavailable content and weaken the privacy boundary. The remaining Conversations work is large enough to require independently verifiable backend and UI/export slices.
changes: Split P6-A01 into P6-A01A for tenant-scoped metadata, permission-separated operational detail, normalized timeline and operator notes, followed by P6-A01B for bounded exports, retained-audio semantics and the Angular workspace.

Do not reconstruct transcripts from routine events, tool logs or provider payloads. Report transcript and audio as unavailable unless a future consent-bound retained-content record exists and remains within approved retention.
Expose content-bearing tool, review, event and note fields only behind conversations.read_content with recent MFA; metadata endpoints return structural status and identifiers only.
Link existing escalation cases and workflow references by source session rather than creating duplicate conversation-owned case or workflow state.
Store operator notes in a tenant-scoped table with forced RLS and preserve authorship/timestamps; privacy execution must treat note content as controlled session content before production activation.
validatedAmendments.approvedBy: User instruction to evaluate and update the plan when repository evidence identifies a safer or more accurate design

validatedAmendments.reason: Repository validation found that the Business Manager property PDF is a property-version cache shared by booking deliveries and contains property inputs rather than the visitor's booking identity. Personal data resides in command-linked booking, delivery and email-command rows. Deleting the cached report would damage unrelated business evidence without fulfilling the subject request. Runtime metering and audit rows are likewise deliberately immutable and schema-limited, while automatic retention cannot safely cover sessions lacking a durable subject binding or completed provider cleanup.
changes: De-identify command-linked Business Manager booking, email-command and delivery fields through a dedicated owner API; retain booking/workflow/property-report state and do not delete the shared property report cache.
Require the exact bm:real-estate:privacy:write scope for Business Manager access/redaction. The legacy broad integration token cannot authorise this operation.
Redact Runtime session metadata, tool/event/review payloads, provider snapshots, raw errors and escalation content while preserving schema-limited usage, audit, command/status and timing evidence.

Keep provider and backup targets blocked until an approved not-stored assessment or verifiable owner evidence is recorded. A blocked external target cannot be represented as completed by the Runtime processor.

Run retention only from an explicitly approved duration and only for closed, subject-bound, non-held sessions with safe provider cleanup. Unbound or cleanup-unsafe candidates keep the run blocked; held candidates are counted and never processed.
Keep provider fallback disabled until equivalent data-flow restrictions are implemented and verified for every fallback profile.
validatedAmendments.approvedBy: User instruction to evaluate and update the plan when repository evidence identifies a safer or more accurate design

validatedAmendments.reason: Repository validation found no universal deletion API or ownership boundary spanning Runtime session evidence, Business Manager generated documents, provider-held data and backups. It also found no approved statutory/business retention durations or legal-review evidence. Treating those stores as synchronously controlled, inventing retention periods or marking external deletion complete from a Runtime database update would create false compliance evidence.
changes: Split P6-03 into P6-03A privacy control/evidence and P6-03B verified execution adapters so the task remains in progress until a rollback-only synthetic request proves each controlled target.
Persist only a tenant-bound digest of an opaque subject reference, require tenant-owned session selectors and separate request verification from execution.

Represent Runtime-controlled and external-owner targets separately. Business Manager documents, provider-owned data and backups remain pending or blocked until their owning adapter returns verifiable evidence; Runtime must not claim their deletion.

Keep automatic retention execution disabled even when policies are recorded. Enable it only after every affected store has an approved processor, legal-hold enforcement and backup handling; do not seed a duration.

Constrain session raw-audio recording, full-transcript persistence and marketing off in the database, and reject a v2 data policy requesting recording or full transcript persistence before provider allocation until an explicit consent activation path exists.
Require production legal checklist state to remain required, pending or independently reviewed with a reference; an administrator cannot self-certify legal approval.
validatedAmendments.approvedBy: User instruction to evaluate and update the plan when repository evidence identifies a safer or more accurate design

validatedAmendments.reason: Repository validation found that the existing admin audit table had neither RLS nor database immutability, metadata redaction was shallow, and no approved retention duration, legal-hold policy, export worker or private export object store exists. An API-only tenant filter, invented deletion schedule or falsely asynchronous archive would weaken the evidence boundary.
changes: Apply FORCE RLS and append-only triggers to the existing audit ledger, revoke Runtime update/delete authority and re-redact historical metadata recursively at every list/detail/export boundary.

Record allowed and failed privileged Admin requests with actor, route/target, permission, outcome and correlation metadata without persisting request bodies, raw errors or query values; preserve existing domain-specific audit events.

Deliver bounded JSON export manifests pinned to immutable filters and an as-of cutoff, capped at 5,000 rows, expiring after 24 hours and rendered from the immutable ledger on authorised access with a SHA-256 digest.
Keep automatic deletion and legal-hold automation disabled and report policyStatus=unavailable until an approved retention/hold policy exists.
Grant audit.export to Organisation Owner behind the existing recent-MFA requirement; retain audit.read without export for Read-only Auditor.
validatedAmendments.approvedBy: User instruction to evaluate and update the plan when repository evidence identifies a safer or more accurate design

validatedAmendments.reason: Repository validation found only test-scoped synthetic capability fixtures and mocked/offline provider protocol tests. Shipping those fixtures or representing their output as live provider evidence would violate their quarantine and overstate production assurance. No approved evaluation data policy, live-provider authority or evaluation spend budget exists.
changes: Reuse the production agent publication-check contract as the deterministic evaluator instead of importing test-only portability fixtures or creating a second execution framework.

Version tenant datasets as bounded publication-check cases, pin evaluator/configuration/target versions, label evidence deterministic and persist immutable results with externalEffects=false and meteredSessionCreated=false.

Gate agent publication only when an approved dataset version is explicitly required, and require a passing run for the exact current draft revision. Draft edits invalidate prior evidence by construction.

Keep live/provider-judged runs unavailable until separate authority, approved data handling and budget gates exist. Mocked-provider contract evidence must remain explicitly labelled and cannot satisfy this deterministic production-publication gate.
Grant Configuration Editor evaluations.read/edit/run while preserving evaluation approval and publication-policy binding for Release Publisher.
validatedAmendments.approvedBy: User instruction to evaluate and update the plan when repository evidence identifies a safer or more accurate design

validatedAmendments.reason: Repository validation found that safe workflow retry and separate escalation delivery/transfer states already exist, while sessions and generic tool calls are not replay-safe. No approved tenant budget, provider cost table, commercial rate card or executable callback/live-transfer adapter exists. Adding generic retry buttons, treating a request as transfer completion, or fabricating budget-exhaustion alerts would weaken existing safety and evidence semantics.
changes: Reuse the existing tenant-scoped, compiled-owner, idempotency-gated workflow retry and leased provider cleanup reconciliation. Expose retry capability status but keep generic session and tool-call retry unavailable.

Persist provider usage as deduplicated source events with provider-independent dimensions, explicit incomplete/estimated/measured status, optional versioned provider-cost estimates and optimistic forward-only reconciliation. Provider cost is never a customer charge.

Make measured usage database-immutable, revoke Runtime DELETE/TRUNCATE authority and enforce FORCE RLS. Record missing final provider usage as incomplete so it can be reconciled rather than silently counted as zero.

Expose tenant operational status and threshold signals for queue age, orphan sessions, failures and denial spikes. Report budget exhaustion as unavailable until P6-A05 supplies an approved tenant budget and commercial policy.

Keep the internal operations inbox as the only supported handoff destination. Callback request, notification acceptance and verified live connection remain distinct states and unavailable without executable adapters.
validatedAmendments.approvedBy: User instruction to evaluate and update the plan when repository evidence identifies a safer or more accurate design

validatedAmendments.reason: Repository validation found no platform-operator organisation provisioning/context-exchange surface and no Admin authoring API or screen for the foundational business, provider and experience profiles. The delivered Admin modules select pre-published dependencies, while v2 browser session evidence remains gated by the managed kiosk broker. Claiming a complete greenfield synthetic-organisation onboarding journey would therefore be false and would encourage bypassing the existing authority boundaries.
changes: Treat P6-01 as the integration gate for an existing authorised tenant whose foundational profiles were provisioned through the owning operational control plane; do not claim platform organisation provisioning or foundational-profile authoring in the current Admin UI.
Add one tenant-scoped, permission-masked persisted readiness endpoint and Admin overview that aggregate the delivered configuration modules without exposing counts for modules the caller cannot read.

Correct the fixed-role matrix exposed by the integrated journey: include escalation-policy read access in the shared configuration-read boundary and grant escalation policy authoring to Configuration Editor. Keep escalation case assignment/resolution with Operations Member and do not grant Organisation Owner edit authority.

Return activationReady only when the caller has complete read visibility. Track pinned v2 session evidence separately from publication readiness so an unrun live session does not become publication authority.

Keep future conversations, evaluations, analytics, audit-log browsing and usage/billing workspaces explicitly planned as P6-A01 through P6-A05 instead of inferring completion from navigation or audit rows.

Verify composition through existing persisted module services, focused readiness/UI tests and a rollback-only least-privilege database check. Do not allocate a live provider, invoke external business effects or write synthetic data to the configured shared database as hidden integration evidence.
validatedAmendments.approvedBy: User instruction to evaluate and update the plan when repository evidence identifies a safer or more accurate design

validatedAmendments.reason: Repository validation found that ResourceRef used capabilityBindingId even though capability_bindings has one distinct row per business-profile capability. A resource returned under the catalog grant therefore could not be consumed under the availability or booking grant: the real-estate connector compared two necessarily different capability-binding IDs. Resource provenance must instead use the shared tenant connector binding while operation authorisation continues to use the distinct capability binding.
changes: Scope portable ResourceRef values with connectorBindingId. Keep capabilityBindingId separately in CapabilityContext for per-operation grants, extension schemas, policy and audit.
Require connectors to reject a resource whose connector binding differs from the server-selected context. Overlapping opaque IDs are safe only as the tuple of tenant, connector binding and opaque ID.

Prove the correction with a test-only synthetic laboratory containing two independently configured tenants, different strict extension schemas, overlapping opaque IDs and a tenant without booking authority. Do not register or ship the fixtures as a commercial vertical or production dataset.

Run one canonical capability harness against both neutral fixture ports and the compiled real-estate connector ports. Add a dedicated Core portability typecheck that has no concrete real-estate registration or provider adapter entrypoint.

Treat the existing mocked-protocol OpenAI, Claude and Gemini suites as offline reasoning portability evidence because all three execute the same ReasoningProvider, canonical tool definitions and secured pipeline contract. Identical provider wording and live success are not required or claimed.
validatedAmendments.approvedBy: User instruction to evaluate and update the plan when repository evidence identifies a safer design

validatedAmendments.reason: Current Google documentation identifies gemini-3.8-live as the stable low-latency audio model, but its response modality is audio, asynchronous NON_BLOCKING function execution is the default, ephemeral tokens and the Live API remain preview surfaces, direct clients use v1beta constrained WebSockets, and session resumption stores text/audio/video conversation state for up to 24 hours. The API also warns that WebSocket connections may reset around ten minutes. Using model defaults, claiming text-output parity, enabling resumption without a reviewed retention decision, or advertising long sessions would violate Sophia's review ordering and data claims.
changes: Implement Gemini Live as a separate NativeRealtimeProvider and v2 lifecycle adapter. Keep the existing OpenAI realtime experiences untouched; Gemini is selectable only through an explicitly published gemini-live-v1 provider binding.

Mint one-use short-lived tokens on the server and constrain them to models/gemini-3.8-live, server-owned instructions, the exact tool catalog, audio response, input/output transcription, barge-in policy and context compression. Never expose GEMINI_API_KEY to the browser.

Set every custom function declaration to BLOCKING. Provider calls still cross the untrusted browser bridge and execute through the authenticated tenant-scoped dispatcher; booking.prepare continues to return explicit UI review rather than treating voice as trusted confirmation.

Use direct v1beta constrained WebSockets with PCM16 little-endian mono input resampled to 16 kHz and 24 kHz output. Process all audio parts, validate the Google endpoint, map adapter-local tool aliases, deduplicate calls, clear Web Audio playback on interruption and suppress responses for provider-cancelled calls.

Do not enable SessionResumptionConfig in this first adapter, preserving the documented Live zero-data-footprint condition for conversation state. Cap published sessions at 540 seconds and token message acceptance at 600 seconds so planned closure precedes the documented approximate ten-minute reset boundary. Longer resumable sessions require a separate field-mask, reconnection and retention design.

Keep the adapter absent from published profiles and fail closed without GEMINI_API_KEY. Production publication additionally requires paid-project and abuse-monitoring review, an approved regional/DPA assessment, preview-risk acceptance, AI-voice disclosure and a credentialed audio/tool/interruption smoke test.

Treat the compiled Angular Gemini transport as a browser adapter implementation, not proof that the current kiosk can select it. The active kiosk facade remains on its bounded v1 session response until the P4 managed credential broker and v2 descriptor/bootstrap translation are activated.
validatedAmendments.approvedBy: User instruction to evaluate and update the plan when repository evidence identifies a safer design

validatedAmendments.reason: The verified OpenAI file-transcription API accepts a completed audio turn rather than an ongoing microphone stream, while the speech API streams raw 24 kHz signed 16-bit little-endian PCM. The existing LiveAvatar and Simli server sendAudioChunk methods are no-ops owned by browser SDK sessions, so treating either as a verified generic audio sink would create a false compatibility claim. A safe first composition therefore needs a bounded-turn transcription adapter, an explicit server audio path and a direct AudioOutputSink contract; low-latency live transcription and avatar injection remain separately gated replacements behind those ports.
changes: Use one memory-bounded client-delimited PCM16 turn, wrap it as WAV and call /v1/audio/transcriptions with configurable gpt-transcribe by default. This baseline emits final transcripts only and does not claim live partial-transcript latency.
Stream /v1/audio/speech with configurable gpt-4o-mini-tts and voice, normalize output to pcm-s16le-24000-mono, preserve sample alignment across HTTP chunks and cap total output bytes.

Make backend audio traversal explicit: microphone turn audio reaches Sophia Runtime and OpenAI transcription; synthesized audio returns through Sophia Runtime to exactly one direct or verified avatar AudioOutputSink. Sophia does not persist the raw audio, but provider handling remains subject to the approved deployment data assessment.

Associate transcription, reasoning, synthesis and sink output with an application turn epoch. Interruption aborts provider work, clears the sole sink's queued audio and discards all late events; it cannot retract audio already heard.

Remove speech-output from the generic LiveAvatar registration until a real audio-injection sink is implemented and contract-tested. Keep Simli avatar-only for the same reason; legacy browser-SDK session behavior is not evidence of server-side sink compatibility.

Keep this internal composition disconnected from a public browser route until the managed kiosk broker supplies authenticated media transport and an approved disclosure tells users the voice is AI-generated.

Record current OpenAI endpoint controls accurately: audio transcription has no documented abuse-monitoring or application-state retention, while audio speech has documented 30-day abuse-monitoring retention and no application-state retention; both are ZDR-eligible. Revalidate these controls and regional routing at deployment time.
validatedAmendments.approvedBy: User instruction to evaluate and update the plan when repository evidence identifies a safer design

validatedAmendments.reason: Current Google documentation makes the post-May-2026 Interactions steps schema the durable API shape, enables server-side interaction storage by default, requires stateless clients to replay all model-generated steps including encrypted thought signatures, documents a supported JSON Schema subset whose unsupported properties may otherwise be ignored, and permits parallel function calls without exposing an OpenAI-equivalent parallel-call disable flag. Treating canonical transcript history as sufficient continuation, relying on default storage, forwarding arbitrary schema constraints, or assuming provider-side single-call ordering would be unsafe.
changes: Use the Gemini Interactions steps/SSE contract behind ReasoningProvider, pin the 2026-05-20 API revision header, and keep the stable model ID configurable server-side.

findings.title: Review/confirmation authority is ephemeral
findings.observation: The baseline reports in-memory maps and frontend flags.
findings.decision: Persist a generic action review and require trusted confirmation evidence, stable action identity and authoritative business idempotency.

findings.title: Tenant authority needs a real binding model
findings.observation: A fixed SOPHIA_RUNTIME_COMPANY_ID and hardcoded kiosk identifiers cannot be assumed to provide multi-tenant isolation.
findings.decision: Initially enforce the existing one-to-one mapping; add scoped connector bindings before admitting more tenants.

findings.title: Existing configuration is not used for session selection
findings.observation: ai_configs exists but session creation does not resolve it.
findings.decision: Introduce active validated profiles and preserve old rows until a verified migration retires them.

findings.title: Tool audit cannot explain failures or true latency
findings.observation: Only successful calls are recorded and timing begins after execution.
findings.decision: Persist lifecycle transitions before execution, with redacted error records and monotonic duration measurement.

findings.title: Kiosk page mixes presentation, vendors and business flows
findings.observation: The page contains provider and domain orchestration.
findings.decision: Extract a session facade, adapter registry, shared presentation contracts and optional pack renderers.

findings.title: Student implementation conflicts with the requested product scope
findings.observation: Student tools, views, source rules, booking paths and workers are intertwined with the current product.
findings.decision: Remove from new-product activation/import graphs and quarantine legacy responsibilities without breaking shared workers.

findings.title: Remote tool provisioning is in customer startup
findings.observation: Tavus tools may be listed or updated in the first session per process.
findings.decision: Provision verified versioned tool catalogs out of band; customer startup performs read-only readiness checks.

findings.title: Business queues are assets worth preserving
findings.observation: Durable report and delivery jobs already exist.
findings.decision: Harden leases/idempotency and expose a normalized status port; do not replace them with SQS immediately.

findings.title: Node.js support needs immediate inspection
findings.observation: Business Manager and workers are reported on Node 20; Node’s current release table marks that line EOL.
findings.decision: Inspect the actual containers; move unsupported execution units to a verified supported LTS in a separately tested change.

findings.title: Exactly-once wording overstates the guarantee
findings.observation: Provider callbacks, HTTP retries and worker claims span independent systems.
findings.decision: Promise idempotent committed effects only where the authoritative connector supports them; otherwise expose outcome_unknown and reconcile.

findings.title: Runtime versions and security controls are reported, not proven
findings.observation: The upload is a snapshot description, not source code or an executed security assessment.
findings.decision: Verify manifest versions, actual guards, transaction scopes and command scripts in P0.

codexExecution.firstRunPrompt: Read sophia-realtime-codex-implementation-plan.v2.1.json and the applicable repository AGENTS.md files. Inspect the actual backend/frontend repositories and current branches, preserve uncommitted work, verify commands and versions, add deterministic real-estate characterization tests, map the student-agency quarantine boundary, audit the existing Admin/auth/knowledge/billing surfaces against all sixteen modules, and create the repository audit, Admin scope/permissions matrix and progress checkpoint. Do not rewrite the application, port student-agency code, run live providers, send emails, charge or modify live subscriptions, apply production migrations or change production behavior. workflowRules: Respect existing repository instructions and user work. Never use git reset --hard, clean, force-push or an unsolicited checkout of the old snapshot.
Do not create a parallel toy codebase to claim the existing application has been migrated.
One task per reviewable patch by default. If a task is too large, split it into named dependent substeps and record partial status without claiming completion.
Use existing package manager and lockfiles; inspect actual scripts before invoking them. Do not blindly install latest dependencies or upgrade frameworks.
Work in a task branch/worktree only where permitted; no changes to live deployment configuration by default.
Make test fixtures synthetic and non-sensitive; never copy live customer data into prompts, fixtures or logs.
Test reads and writes against isolated local/disposable services. Never send real email, create real bookings or allocate metered sessions as a hidden test step.
Missing provider keys does not prevent adapter implementation and offline tests, but blocks live-production capability claims.
Keep a support-window compatibility layer; never leave a security bypass for legacy browser provider fields.
Do not weaken tests, policies or tenant checks simply to make a provider integration pass.
Do not extract generic code from the student/migration implementation. Use shared contracts and independent implementations where needed.
A provider-specific library may accelerate an adapter but may not become the domain/tool/state model for the whole platform.
Do not introduce external plugin/MCP/code execution merely to make tools generic.
Document unresolved assumptions at their task boundary and continue independent safe work; essential auth/access barriers remain blockers.
After each task record actual checks and remaining risks. Never report a test, migration or live smoke that was not run.
For Admin work, consult the matching module criteria. Do not replace persisted functionality with mock screens or silently expand user roles, provider access, payment authority or recording consent.
When adopting v2.1 after v2 work, preserve completed work and record new acceptance gaps; do not reset branches or repeat completed business mutations.

toolInvocation.identity: Provider call IDs deduplicate transport delivery, not business intent. Mutations use a stable action/command ID tied to the durable review and authoritative request hash.

toolResult.display: Typed blocks such as item-list, detail-card, media-gallery, availability-list, review-card, operation-status and source-list. Business packs can register schema-validated custom renderers.
toolResult.spokenSummary: Derived from validated authoritative state with privacy minimisation; never report a booking or delivery solely because the model says it succeeded.
toolResult.sources: Tenant/connector/source identifiers, retrieval time, freshness and access classification. No public-source substitution for missing private business facts.
toolResult.outputRule: Validate and minimise connector output before returning it to any model; untrusted retrieved text must remain data, not instructions.

canonicalConversationEvent.stateRule: Keep completed user/assistant/tool records as portable application history. Track interrupted output and playback checkpoints where available. Provider opaque continuation state remains inside the adapter and is never treated as portable text.
canonicalConversationEvent.safetyRule: A provider or browser event cannot authorise a mutation merely by labelling itself confirmed. Provenance, sequence and review binding must be verified.
canonicalConversationEvent.retentionBoundary: Canonical history may be transient during a live session. Full transcript persistence is disabled by default; durable audit stores minimised operational events and separately governed confirmation evidence, not all transcript payloads.

compositionValidation: Each capability has one declared owner; reject incompatible or duplicate ownership.
Exactly one audible speech output path per turn. Do not play native model audio and avatar-generated speech simultaneously.
Reject an avatar requiring audio input when only text input is available, unless an explicit synthesis adapter bridges it.
Reject voice-required profiles without verified speech input/output and interruption support; offer an explicitly allowed text fallback.
Native/composite sessions do not accept an independent reasoning override unless the adapter explicitly supports that operation.
Verify codec/sample-rate/frame compatibility and approved transcoding before allocation.
Check language support, data-handling approval, regional constraints, cost ceiling, quota and health before allocation.
Check availability of trustworthy tool/confirmation evidence; require the secure UI confirmation path when voice evidence cannot be established.

routingAndFallback.default: Pin a resolved plan for the whole session; evaluate health and authorised fallbacks before creating resources.
routingAndFallback.midSession: Do not silently swap provider. Quiesce the turn, reconcile pending actions, close the old resources, create a new session with explicitly permitted minimal canonical context, and explain a reconnect where necessary.
routingAndFallback.privacy: Fallback must satisfy the same tenant data policy; a cheaper/available provider cannot silently change processing jurisdictions or retention.
routingAndFallback.state: Never transfer provider-private credentials or continuation state to another vendor. Revalidate or expire existing action reviews on restart/configuration changes.

providerStrategy.mediaTopology: Prefer direct browser media where the chosen provider supports a secure connection plus trusted server control. An orchestrated STT/LLM/TTS pipeline may legitimately require a server WebSocket/media adapter. Do not force every provider through the same WebRTC design or assert NestJS never handles audio. Keep media handling in an isolated module that can later scale independently.
providerStrategy.lifecycle: Track each allocated provider resource durably with a cleanup owner/lease; compensate partial startup, reconcile orphan sessions, enforce maximum session duration and make close repeatable. Retain only non-secret resource identifiers.
providerStrategy.toolProvisioning: Version and hash provider tool catalogs during deployment or an explicit controlled job. Use separate tenant/environment provider resources where prompt/tool attachments are mutable; never update a shared PAL in a way that changes another tenant’s active permissions.
providerStrategy.researchBoundary: Extract researchBusiness behind ResearchProvider without inheriting student rules. Enable only where the tenant explicitly approves sources/purpose. A public web search is never a fallback for missing private catalog, price, availability or policy data.

transitions: prepare -> retrieve current resource/slot -> canonicalise and persist payload -> render the same authoritative payload
presentation acknowledgement -> presented; presentation is not confirmation
subsequent explicit user interaction -> verify user channel, review/session ownership, hash, ordering and expiry -> confirmed
confirmed -> transactionally claim executing with stable command ID -> call business connector
business success/receipt -> succeeded; authoritative conflict -> invalidate and present alternatives
network timeout after submission -> outcome_unknown -> query same command receipt; never create a new command to guess-retry
payload/resource/policy change or expired review -> invalidated/expired -> require a new review and new explicit approval
reviewStateMachine.confirmationEvidence: An authenticated confirmation-button action or trusted server-observed user turn correlated after presentation. A model-produced flag, model tool argument, frontend in-memory state, or unverified browser-forwarded transcript is insufficient.
reviewStateMachine.voiceFallback: If the active transport cannot provide trustworthy voice-turn evidence, require the explicit secure confirmation UI rather than weakening authorisation.
reviewStateMachine.tokenNote: A signed short-lived review token can reference the durable record; it does not itself prove the user approved it. Persist replay/consumption state.

commandIdempotency.sameKeySamePayload: Return the original committed receipt or current processing state.
commandIdempotency.sameKeyDifferentPayload: Reject with CONFLICT; never overwrite the original command.
commandIdempotency.businessTransaction: At the authoritative service, validate tenant/resource, acquire appropriate capacity locks or constraints, persist mutation + command receipt + initial queue/outbox rows in one transaction.
commandIdempotency.capacityRule: Respect actual slot semantics. An inspection may have capacity greater than one; do not impose a universal unique-slot constraint. Test both capacity-one and multi-capacity resources.
commandIdempotency.runtimeBusinessBoundary: Runtime review state and Business Manager booking commit are separate transactions. Recovery queries the authoritative receipt using the same command ID.
commandIdempotency.unsupportedConnectors: A connector without safe idempotent writes or a reliable reconciliation strategy must be read-only or require an explicitly approved manual path.
commandIdempotency.deliverySemantics: Callbacks, jobs and requests may repeat. Guarantee deduplication/idempotent effects within declared boundaries, not universal exactly-once execution.
commandIdempotency.cancellationRule: A user interruption/abort can stop pending local work or unplayed speech. After an authoritative mutation is submitted, do not mark it cancelled unless cancellation is acknowledged by that system; otherwise reconcile it as processing/outcome_unknown. Never cancel an already committed booking implicitly.

boundary.tenantAdmin: Manage the selected organisation within membership, entitlements and role grants. Cannot install arbitrary code, add unapproved providers, change platform safeguards or see another organisation.
boundary.application: Prefer one protected lazy-loaded Angular Admin area with backend Admin modules. Do not create a new product database, identity directory or duplicate business service unless P0 provides a documented reason.
boundary.businessNeutrality: Use capability/schema registries and versioned bindings. Real estate supplies only optional pack-specific forms/templates/schema extensions. Student-agency code remains excluded.
boundary.providerNeutrality: Show capabilities, validated profiles and registered adapters. Concrete vendor setup forms derive from approved adapter schemas; no UI/controller switch over provider names.
boundary.identity: Reuse verified existing identity records and auth boundary; add membership/roles where absent. Public runtime tokens cannot access Admin.
boundary.configurationVsBusinessTruth: Publishing freezes configuration references, not live catalog/inventory/availability. Existing Business Manager records remain authoritative.
boundary.mvpNotNoCode: Full named module coverage means bounded useful management workflows, not a workflow-canvas, arbitrary script tools or unrestricted custom roles.

proposedArchitecture.pathRule: Proposed routes only; verify established Admin URL/versioning conventions during P0 before adopting. Keep public runtime and privileged Admin authentication separated.
apiRules: Version DTOs and validate all writes.
Enforce tenant/resource permissions server-side; UI guards are not authority.
Use ETags/revision checks on edited resources and idempotency where actions can be replayed.
Paginate/filter list APIs and bound/export asynchronously where appropriate.
Return redacted DTOs; no long-lived secrets.
Record administrator decisions and sensitive content access.

suggestedMvpRoleTemplates.name: Organisation owner
suggestedMvpRoleTemplates.purpose: Tenant governance and membership; protected final owner. No platform privilege.

suggestedMvpRoleTemplates.name: Configuration editor
suggestedMvpRoleTemplates.purpose: Draft agent, instructions, knowledge and permitted bindings; no publishing by default.

suggestedMvpRoleTemplates.name: Release publisher
suggestedMvpRoleTemplates.purpose: Validate/publish/rollback within approved grants; cannot assign themselves broader permissions.

suggestedMvpRoleTemplates.name: Operations member
suggestedMvpRoleTemplates.purpose: Read permitted operational metadata and act on assigned escalations; content/export grants separate.

suggestedMvpRoleTemplates.name: Billing administrator
suggestedMvpRoleTemplates.purpose: Read/manage approved tenant commercial settings and portal access; no default transcript or publishing rights.

suggestedMvpRoleTemplates.name: Read-only auditor
suggestedMvpRoleTemplates.purpose: Read permitted metadata/audit; exports and personal content require separate grants.

adminWorkstream.roleNote: Proposed fixed MVP templates to validate against current roles in P0. Permissions, not role-name checks in domain code, enforce authority.

modules.name: Organisations
modules.v2Coverage: Partial: tenant identity, profiles and minimal operator configuration exist in the plan; no explicit full organisation lifecycle screen.
uiDeliverables: Organisation list for authorised platform operators; an ordinary tenant member sees only organisations they belong to.
Create/onboard, view, edit branding/timezone/language settings, suspend admission and resume; no default destructive delete.
Organisation switcher and optional locations, with explicit active-tenant context.
backendDeliverables: Map the existing runtime customer record to an organisation; verify ownership rather than duplicating it.
Validate permitted profile fields, publish configuration through versioned APIs and block new sessions on suspension without cancelling committed business jobs.
Separate platform organisation provisioning from tenant settings permissions.
acceptanceCriteria: Switching an organisation invalidates old cached tenant data.
A tenant admin cannot enumerate unrelated organisations.
Suspension does not delete bookings, reports, receipts or historical records.

modules.name: Users
modules.v2Coverage: Insufficient: authenticated membership and roles are required, but invitation, membership administration and user lifecycle tasks are not specified.
uiDeliverables: List tenant members and pending invitations; invite, revoke invitation, update permitted role, suspend/remove membership.
Show invitation expiry and MFA/account status only where the existing identity integration supports them.
Distinguish removing tenant access from globally deleting an identity.
backendDeliverables: Reuse verified existing identities; add tenant memberships/invitations only where absent.
Hash invitation tokens, bind them to recipient and tenant, set expiry and single-use redemption; no plaintext invitation tokens in logs.
Prevent privilege escalation and removal of the final organisation owner; invalidate relevant access on revocation.
acceptanceCriteria: Expired, replayed and wrong-recipient invitation redemption fails.
A tenant member cannot grant platform-admin access.
Revoked membership cannot keep accessing the previous tenant via an old session or refresh path.

modules.name: Agents
modules.v2Coverage: Partial: server-owned agent/profile configuration and minimal controls are explicit, but an agent management workspace is not.
uiDeliverables: List, create draft, edit, clone within the same tenant, enable/disable and archive an agent.
Configure display identity, languages, allowed experiences, capability bindings and escalation/knowledge references.
Show readiness validation and a sandbox test entry point.
backendDeliverables: Agent identity is independent of industry, provider and presentation avatar.
Draft changes do not mutate active sessions; enablement requires a published validated release.
Validate all referenced resources belong to the tenant and are within granted entitlements.
acceptanceCriteria: A configured neutral agent and the real-estate agent use the same Admin APIs.
Cross-tenant cloning or binding is rejected.
Changing providers does not require a different agent entity.

modules.name: Agent versions
modules.v2Coverage: Partial: immutable profile versions and publication/rollback are explicit; history, diff and complete release-manifest management are not.
uiDeliverables: Version history, draft-versus-published diff, validation results, publish, retire and rollback to a previous approved release.
Display author, timestamps, release notes and evaluation/approval evidence.
Identify the exact release used by a conversation.
backendDeliverables: Publish an immutable release manifest referencing instructions, knowledge snapshot/revisions, capabilities, connector bindings, workflow versions, experience/provider policy and permissions.
Pin the resolved manifest and configuration hash on session creation; separately recheck emergency revocations.
Use optimistic concurrency on drafts; resolve what versioned rollback means for knowledge availability and connector health.
acceptanceCriteria: Concurrent edits cannot silently overwrite another draft.
A rollback affects future sessions but does not rewrite history or repeat committed commands.
Live inventory and availability remain authoritative live data, not frozen by the configuration manifest.

modules.name: Instructions
modules.v2Coverage: Not explicitly covered as an Admin editor: prompts/instructions exist as runtime concerns, not an authoring and publication module.
uiDeliverables: Edit tenant-owned instructions, tone, greeting, language behaviour and permitted variables.
Preview the resolved instruction composition without exposing secrets; compare revisions and test a draft.
Show which platform safety rules are non-editable.
backendDeliverables: Separate immutable platform controls from tenant-authored content and pack terminology.
Validate a declared variable schema; never evaluate arbitrary template code.
Version instructions as an agent release dependency; prompts never grant permissions, enable recording or authorise tools.
acceptanceCriteria: An instruction requesting hidden tools does not expand capability grants.
Unpublished text cannot affect a production conversation.
An unsupported template variable fails validation clearly.

modules.name: Knowledge
modules.v2Coverage: Partial: approved knowledge/search and connector isolation are included; source ingestion, approval, version and reindex management are not.
uiDeliverables: Manage approved text/file sources and supported connector-source references; show draft/processing/ready/failed/retired states.
Review extracted text, source metadata, revisions, agent assignments and ingestion errors before publication.
Test retrieval against a chosen draft/release; provide safe reindex/retire actions and freshness information.
backendDeliverables: Use tenant-scoped durable ingestion jobs, bounded parsing and approved storage access; validate type/size, scan files and isolate parsers.
Search only published approved source revisions under the requester's grants; retrieved text remains untrusted data.
Do not introduce an arbitrary URL crawler. Remote sources require a separately approved connector with SSRF and egress controls.
Keep retrieval and optional embedding services behind adapters; do not hardcode a model or copy student-agency retrieval code.
acceptanceCriteria: An unpublished or another tenant's document is never retrieved.
A malicious, oversized or unsupported file is rejected or quarantined, not executed.
Retiring a source blocks future retrieval as policy requires without rewriting historic audit metadata.

modules.name: Tools
modules.v2Coverage: Partial: tool registry, policies and capability enablement exist; an inspectable tool management surface is not explicit.
uiDeliverables: Catalog of approved registered tool versions, descriptions, input/output schemas, risk level and required permission/confirmation.
Enable/bind permitted tools per agent and preview policy decisions.
Sandbox test using synthetic data only; show health and recent failure indicators.
backendDeliverables: Expose a read-only registry description and controlled tenant binding APIs.
Only approved compiled tools are selectable; no UI for arbitrary SQL, code or unrestricted HTTP.
Agent grants are bounded by organisation/platform grants and checked server-side on every invocation.
acceptanceCriteria: A UI checkbox cannot bypass a mandatory confirmation policy.
A direct API call cannot enable an unapproved registration.
Sandbox testing cannot create a real booking or send a real email.

modules.name: Connectors
modules.v2Coverage: Partial: tenant-to-account bindings and credential references are explicit; connection lifecycle, onboarding and health screens are not.
uiDeliverables: Approved connector catalog, account binding wizard, scopes, health, sync status and safe connection test.
Reconnect/rotate/disconnect controls with affected-agent warnings.
Use a provider-hosted OAuth connection where supported or secure server-side credential submission; never reveal stored credentials.
backendDeliverables: Validate account/company identity and requested scopes on both sides.
OAuth state/PKCE and callback handling apply where supported; otherwise use the verified secure credential mechanism.
Credentials stay in a secret backend; browser responses show only safe references/status.
Document in-flight command reconciliation before disconnect/revocation.
acceptanceCriteria: Another tenant's account cannot be selected through a forged ID.
Read APIs, exports and routine logs never return long-lived connector secrets.
Disconnect cannot silently report a submitted mutation as cancelled.

modules.name: Workflows
modules.v2Coverage: Partial: durable workflow execution, reports/delivery and operational retry are planned; workflow configuration and version screens are not.
uiDeliverables: List approved workflow templates; configure allowed parameters, trigger bindings, conditions and approval requirements using schema-driven forms.
Version, validate, assign and enable a configured workflow; inspect run/step status.
Show safe retry controls only where an implementation declares retry/reconciliation support.
backendDeliverables: Build on compiled template registries and existing durable workers; do not build a general-purpose drag-and-drop code/workflow engine.
Pin a workflow version per execution and preserve command identity/authoritative receipts.
Keep the sale-report extension in the real-estate pack, not in the generic Admin/runtime workflow logic.
acceptanceCriteria: Template parameters cannot expand tool permissions or remove required confirmation.
A new workflow version does not mutate a running report job.
Repeated manual retries cannot create duplicate business mutations.

modules.name: Permissions
modules.v2Coverage: Partial: tenant authorisation, role checks and privileged MFA are required; a permissions matrix/assignment workspace is not.
uiDeliverables: Inspect role-permission matrix and effective grants; assign approved roles within the organisation.
Show user administration, agent editing, publishing, transcript viewing, exports and billing as distinct permissions.
Expose platform support access as separate, time-bound and auditable rather than implicit impersonation.
backendDeliverables: Deny by default and enforce permissions at each API/resource boundary; route guards are presentation only.
Use a documented registry of fixed MVP roles and permissions; custom role authoring can be deferred without deferring enforcement.
Membership/role changes invalidate access as defined; prevent self-elevation and final-owner removal.
acceptanceCriteria: A read-only user cannot publish via a direct HTTP request.
A publisher cannot grant itself credential or billing administration.
Platform support cannot inspect tenant content without the required explicit support grant.

modules.name: Escalations
modules.v2Coverage: Partial: escalation destinations and durable handoff/callback status are planned; rule management and an operations inbox are not.
uiDeliverables: Configure approved destinations, business hours, rules and response targets.
Escalation inbox with owner, open/assigned/in-progress/resolved states and minimal context.
Distinguish callback requested, notification accepted and verified live transfer.
backendDeliverables: Authorise destination changes and carry minimal necessary conversation context.
Use a durable case/handoff record with delivery/transfer status from the actual connector.
A human transfer request is a reliable escalation path; unsupported transfer channels must remain visibly unavailable.
acceptanceCriteria: An unconfigured channel is not shown as a working live transfer.
Destination changes do not leak case details across tenants.
A requested escalation remains tracked when the original voice session closes.

modules.name: Conversations
modules.v2Coverage: Tenant-scoped filters, permission-separated metadata/content APIs, normalized timeline, workflow/escalation linkage, retention-aware reads, operator notes, bounded expiring render-on-access exports and the Angular workspace are delivered. Transcript/audio remain honestly unavailable because no consent-bound retained assets exist; the fixed Operations Member template intentionally has metadata/annotation but not content/export.
uiDeliverables: Tenant-scoped list filtered by date, agent/release, channel, outcome and escalation status.
Detail timeline with permitted/redacted messages, tool invocations, review/confirmation and workflow links.
Notes, restricted export and escalation linkage; audio playback only where recording was explicitly enabled and retained.
backendDeliverables: Separate metadata visibility from transcript/audio/export permissions.
Paginate and authorise every list/detail/export; escape untrusted transcript text and redact sensitive fields.
Retained transcript content is optional; show unavailable/deleted content honestly and never reconstruct it from routine logs.
acceptanceCriteria: A metadata-only operator cannot retrieve raw transcript through the API.
Opted-out or expired audio cannot be played or exported.
A malicious transcript cannot run script in the Admin UI.

modules.name: Evaluations
modules.v2Coverage: Tenant-facing deterministic datasets, pinned immutable runs/results and exact-draft publication evidence are delivered. Live/provider-judged evaluation remains unavailable pending separate authority, data-policy and budget gates.
uiDeliverables: Create structured deterministic publication-check cases without arbitrary executable payloads.
Run selected draft or immutable release configurations without invoking providers or production connectors and compare their pinned evidence.
Show case failures, evaluator/target versions and unrun publication requirements; attach exact-draft results to publication decisions.
backendDeliverables: Pin dataset, agent target, configuration digest and evaluator versions; separate deterministic checks from unavailable optional model-based judging.
Execute no connector or tool during deterministic evaluation and enforce no external effects or metered sessions in persistence.
Local deterministic checks require no live keys. Live/model-judged runs remain unavailable until approved data policy, provider authority, budget and separate authorisation exist.
acceptanceCriteria: An evaluation cannot call a production mutation connector.
Missing credentials or unrun tests never become a pass.
A failed required publication check cannot be bypassed by changing instruction text.

modules.name: Analytics
modules.v2Coverage: A tenant-scoped dashboard now exposes versioned definitions, denominators, source-confirmed outcomes, filters, timezone/freshness/coverage and separated provider estimates. Bounded aggregate-only JSON snapshots expire after 24 hours and are digest-verified; materialized aggregates remain deferred until scale evidence requires them.
uiDeliverables: Dashboard for conversations, authoritative outcomes, booking/task completion where a pack declares them, escalations, failures and response latency.
Filter by organisation, agent/release, channel and date; show usage/cost alongside outcomes.
Display metric definitions, denominators, timezone, freshness, missing data and estimated values.
backendDeliverables: Derive aggregates from deduplicated canonical events and authoritative completion receipts.
Use capability/pack-declared business outcome definitions, not hardcoded property metrics in core.
Do not claim incremental revenue, staff savings or causal conversion lift without separately supplied evidence.
acceptanceCriteria: Duplicate events do not increase completed-booking counts.
Timezone boundaries and empty/missing data states are tested.
Unknown attribution is labelled, not invented as business benefit.

modules.name: Audit logs
modules.v2Coverage: FORCE-RLS append-only audit evidence, recursive redaction, filterable list/detail access, privileged request outcomes and bounded MFA-gated exports are delivered. Automatic retention deletion and legal-hold automation remain unavailable pending an approved policy.
uiDeliverables: Search/filter by actor, action, target, time, outcome and correlation ID.
Inspect redacted configuration diffs, permission changes, publication and execution decisions.
Restricted bounded export manifests with pinned cutoff, retrieval expiry, digest and export-access audit.
backendDeliverables: Cover administrator reads of sensitive content and writes as well as tool lifecycle events.
Normal application roles cannot alter audit history; use minimal immutable events without embedding unnecessary personal content.
Report retention/hold policy unavailable and keep automatic deletion disabled until an approved policy exists; do not promise unqualified permanent immutability of personal information.
acceptanceCriteria: Sensitive-content views and permission changes create audit events.
Exports remain tenant-scoped and omit secrets.
A routine operator cannot edit/delete history through the Admin API.

modules.name: Usage/Billing
modules.v2Coverage: P6-02 usage evidence plus P6-A05 deliver the protected workspace, read-only versioned commercial model, exact no-charge preview, opaque subscription/invoice references, downward-only tenant guardrails, estimate-only alerts and atomic shared v1/v2 admission. P6-A06A adds a concrete dormant Stripe test-mode adapter, signed payload-free callbacks, replay/stale-event protection, authoritative reconciliation and protected hosted-action readiness. Dedicated configuration and provider sandbox end-to-end evidence remain P6-A06B; live activation remains separately gated.
uiDeliverables: Usage by provider-independent dimensions, cost estimates, incomplete/reconciled status, budgets and quota alerts.
Separate vendor cost from customer charges; show assigned plan, included units, rate-card version, pricing currency and clearly labelled billing preview.
When a billing integration is enabled, show subscription and invoice/payment status; use hosted payment-method/checkout links instead of handling card data.
backendDeliverables: Persist deduplicated usage separately from versioned tenant commercial pricing and billing-provider authoritative records.
Define BillingProvider port for supported subscription, invoice, portal and signed webhook operations; reuse a verified existing provider only through the adapter boundary.
Verify webhook authenticity, tenant/product mapping and replay/out-of-order handling; define reconciliation and entitlement updates.

Do not invent approved prices, currencies, tax treatment or overage policy. Live billing requires explicit commercial/legal approval and verified provider access; keep existing unrelated payments untouched.
acceptanceCriteria: Replayed usage and billing events do not double count or apply entitlements twice.
Estimated supplier cost is never labelled an invoice or final customer charge.
With live billing disabled no operation makes a charge; missing configuration is explicit.
Organisation billing cannot modify Toolkit or unrelated Business Manager payment objects.

releaseManifest.secretRule: Reference secret handles only; never include long-lived secret values in a release, diff or export.

commercialBilling.status: Read-only commercial model, downward-only tenant usage guardrails, estimate-only provider-cost alerts, atomic shared admission and a concrete dormant Stripe test-mode lifecycle are implemented. No dedicated Sophia Stripe credential, recurring Price mapping, portal configuration, webhook destination, provider sandbox end-to-end evidence or live payment configuration is active.
stages: Versioned commercial plans and non-charge previews
Concrete billing adapter and sandbox lifecycle
commercialBilling.billableVsCost: Supplier usage/cost is not customer price. Plans, units, included usage, effective dates, currency, tax and overage treatment need explicit commercial decisions.
commercialBilling.existingPayments: Inspect for reusable adapter primitives but preserve Toolkit and unrelated Business Manager accounts, subscriptions and webhooks in separate product/tenant namespaces.
liveGate: Explicit authorised billing account and production access
Verified signed callback and reconciliation tests
Tenant/product mapping and duplicate/out-of-order event tests
Explicit user authorisation to activate live billing
commercialBilling.blockedWork: Implement independent usage and billing contracts/UI where possible; mark concrete integration or smoke tests blocked/unrun when required access is absent. Do not claim the module production-ready.
commercialBilling.nonChargingPilot: A deliberately no-charge pilot may be approved separately with billing disabled and its readiness exclusions visible. It does not satisfy full commercial billing completion.

moduleDefinitionOfDone: Persisted backend operations exist for the declared bounded scope.
The protected Angular screen uses the real APIs, not mock-only placeholders.
Tenant/role checks and negative tests cover UI and direct APIs.
Configuration changes, sensitive reads and privileged actions emit suitable audit events.
Unit/integration/E2E evidence is recorded; unrun live tests remain explicit.
Provider/business-neutral boundaries and real-estate regression tests still pass.
executionSequence: P0: inspect existing Admin/auth/payments and record reuse/gaps; no behavior changes.
P2: identity/membership/permissions and agent authoring/release APIs.
P3: knowledge, tools/connectors, workflow and escalation management APIs.
P4: protected shell plus configuration screens.
P7: approved cutover; live commercial billing uses an independent activation gate.
adminWorkstream.firstRun: P0 remains the first bounded run. Do not start building all screens or enabling live services merely because this scope is listed.
